title: Rollout Signal Cartographer and Route Compare Lab
creator: Priya Patel
description: Introduce a ‘Signal Cartographer’ and an interactive ‘Route Compare Lab’ inside Redwood Console to help engineers visualize how rollout signals (latency, nll, hallucination rate, cost) propagate across routes, cohorts, and traces. The feature bundles cohort diff heatmaps, route-level metric overlays, linked trace timelines, and a replayable shadow-traffic sandbox that lets teams simulate rollback scenarios before committing changes.
background: Teams frequently struggle to correlate small metric deltas with root causes during canary and A/B rollouts. Current Console panels expose per-route metrics and traces but lack a coordinated, explorable surface that maps signals spatially across routes and cohorts and simulates rollback outcomes. This gap increases MTTI and raises the chance of noisy rollouts slipping through until it impacts customers.
goals: Create a visual map (Signal Cartographer) that surfaces the strongest deviating signals per route and cohort
Provide an interactive comparator (Route Compare Lab) to diff two cohorts across multiple metrics with linked traces
Enable a safe shadow-traffic replay sandbox that can run a historical window and surface likely rollback candidates
Expose a small set of actionable rollback suggestions and confidence scores tied to signal provenance
out_of_scope: Implementing new alerting pipelines (we will reuse existing telemetry and alert infra)
Full automated rollback execution (this project surfaces suggestions; exec is subsequent work)
proposed_solution: Build a Console surface composed of: (1) Signal Cartographer overview — a topology-style grid that ranks routes by composite deviation score; (2) Route Compare Lab — a multi-metric diff view with toggles for time window, metric weights, and a synchronized trace viewer; (3) Shadow Replay Sandbox — a replay runner that can feed past traffic into the candidate variant in a controlled environment and surface divergence metrics and trace diffs. Integrate with rollout metadata (variant ids, trafficsplit) and existing trace links so users can jump from a signal to the exact traces and example requests.
acceptance_criteria: Signal Cartographer displays deviation scores for at least 20 routes and allows sorting/filtering by metric and cohort
Route Compare Lab can generate cohort diffs for latency, token-cost, top-k hallucinations, and user-facing error rate and surface linked traces
Shadow Replay Sandbox can replay a 1-hour window against a candidate variant in a staging cluster and produce a trace-diff summary within 30 minutes
UI includes an explainability panel that lists top 3 contributing signals for any selected route/cohort pair
Documentation and an internal runbook published to Confluence with example workflows and rollback decision checklist
milestones: M2: Backend telemetry adapters + API endpoints (2026-03-29)
M3: Initial UI build for Cartographer (2026-04-06)
M4: Route Compare Lab + trace linking (2026-04-15)
M5: Shadow Replay Sandbox prototype + internal validation (2026-04-25)
M6: Documentation, internal beta, and launch (2026-05-02)
qa_plan: Smoke test on staging with three sample rollouts: (1) latency regression, (2) hallucination increase, (3) increased token cost. Validate that cartographer surfaces the regressing route within top-3 and that trace links open contextual spans. Run replay sandbox against a recorded 1-hour trace and verify aggregate diffs match production telemetry within 5%.
risks: Telemetry volume may make real-time cartography expensive — mitigate with sampling and progressive loading
False positives from noisy signals could erode trust — include confidence scoring and provenance links
Replay sandbox may not perfectly reproduce production side effects; clearly surface limitations
notes: We should prioritize linking example request payloads to traces so PMs/engineers can reproduce failures locally
Consider exposing an API to export cartographer snapshots for runbooks and postmortems
Align metric definitions with Metric Catalog (observability team) to avoid drift
